A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPEAR study. All 25 pages of each version, including Appendices A–G, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures sufficient for reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original SPEAR experiments on LibriSpeech, AudioSet, SUPERB and HEAR, plus component ablations and representation analyses in Section 5 and Appendices C–G.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experimental results, including downstream evaluations, ablations and the controlled comparison with USAD.

M1.justification: The MVQ targets, Zipformer architecture, asymmetric dual-domain objective and token-mixing procedure remain unchanged. Revisions to their motivation and positioning do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: The pre-training corpora in Tables 1–2 and the LibriSpeech, AudioSet, SUPERB and HEAR evaluation coverage are unchanged, including the limited-supervision and out-of-domain appendix evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including WavLM, USAD, BEATs, EAT, ATST-frame, Dasheng and HuBERT, and the Transformer and k-means controls. The expanded discussion introduces no additional evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Splits, metrics, model configurations, training budgets and evaluation procedures are retained. Appendix G still compares 94M models using the same teachers but unequal training corpora of 95.3k and 126k hours; v4's abbreviated summary does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: The token-mixing, domain-fusion, teacher-selection, loss-weighting, architecture, quantisation and codebook analyses are already present in v2. V4 expands their Section 5.4 summary while retaining the same evidence in Appendices F–G.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries and graphical findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 retains SPEARs+a XLarge's LS-960 test-other WER of 2.9 and AS-2M mAP of 50.0. The expanded summaries reuse existing findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of MVQ encoding, reconstruction, training losses, token mixing and CTC decoding are unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same unified-representation, MVQ and token-mixing claims, including surpassing WavLM Large on 12 of 15 SUPERB tasks. Section 5.1 removes a redundant AudioSet state-of-the-art phrase while retaining the corresponding superiority statement and results.

C2.justification: New Section 7 explicitly identifies quantiser training and frozen-teacher target extraction as computational overhead. Its teacher-dependence and generative-scope limitations largely restate Appendices F.1.1 and D. Section 5.4 also describes reduced cross-domain interference more categorically than v2's explanatory attribution in Appendix G.

D1.justification: V4 adds an abstract footnote linking to a Hugging Face collection of SPEAR encoders, whereas v2 only promises release. Implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish actual resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 extends the comparison with MT2KD and USAD by explicitly contrasting their treatment of overlapping sound scenes with SPEAR's token mixing. The cited-work membership is unchanged; the Bregman publication-year update is bibliographic.

P1.justification: Localized revisions expand Section 5.4's short appendix pointers into six explanatory bullets, add Limitations and Acknowledgements, and update affiliation numbering and publication text. Most prose and the appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Publication headers, first-page organization and float placement change; for example, Table 5 moves from page 7 to page 8. All four figures and 26 tables are retained, without substantive graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: V4 modestly improves transparency and readability by explicitly acknowledging computational overhead, summarizing existing appendix findings and supplying a model-access pointer. The experimental and mathematical evidence is unchanged. The more categorical interference explanation adds no causal evidence, limiting the gain to presentation and disclosure.
